When using Flower,
you can change the configuration in three ways:

1. By passing option flags to the CLI, as described in [the CLI
   guide](/docs/guide/cli.qmd).
2. By setting parameters in the Python `Config` class, as described in
   [the Python guide](/docs/guide/python.qmd).
3. By reading from a configuration file on disk, as described below.
<!-- TODO the python file does not exist yet, make sure link is uptaded
if name is different -->

Since there are multiple ways to configure Flower, you might wonder what
happens if the same configuration option is modified in both the CLI (or
Python interface) and then also in the configuration file. In this case,
the option that is passed to the CLI (or Python interface) will take
precedence over what is written in the configuration file. If no value
is specified for an option in either of these locations, Flower will
fall back to the default values listed below.

Note that the CLI and Python interface uniquely specifies which URI to read,
this cannot be set from the configuration file. The CLI and Python
interface are also the only ways to change the configuration for the
`view` subcommand; the configuration file is only read when the `build`
subcommand is used.

## The configuration file

Flower will try to read settings from `.flower.toml`.
If that file does not exist,
Flower will look in `pyproject.toml` instead.
If both files exist, only `.flower.toml` will be read.

### Configurable settings

The following settings can be configured via the configuration file:

`style`
: The style decides how the metadata is structured in the output files.
One of `'quarto-one-page'`, `'quarto-resource-listing'`,
`'quarto-resource-tables'`, or `'custom'`. Default: `'quarto-one-page'`

`output-dir`
: The directory where Flower will save the output files. Default: `'docs/'`

`template-dir`
: The directory that contains the templates files to use when `style='custom'`.
Default: `'templates/'`

To see examples of how the different styles would structure the output,
see [the Outputs documentation](`docs/design/interface/outputs.qmd`).
<!-- TODO change to guide link when available -->
When style is set to `'custom'`,
the structure of the output is determined by a custom set of templates
and configurations explained in [the documentation about custom
styles](../guide/custom-styles.qmd).

### Configuration file syntax

To change the configuration settings from their default values, the
following syntax would be used in `.flower.toml`:

``` {.toml filename=".flower.toml"}
style = "custom"
template-dir = "my-templates/"
output-dir = "my-docs/"
```

If configuring Flower via `pyproject.toml` instead, a heading needs to
be included to indicate where in the file Flower can find the settings:

``` {.toml filename="pyproject.toml"}
[tool.seedcase-flower]
style = "custom"
template_dir = "my-templates/"
output_dir = "my-docs/"
```
